result.text:
I didn't add the ETA cache. I couldn't reproduce the slowness locally, and ETA isn't the cause. All 96 tests pass, including the 2 new ones.

**Why no cache**
- `GET /shipments` calls `calculateEta` only on the returned page. That is 50 items by default and 500 at most, not all 5k. At 50 items it costs about 0.6 ms.
- On a 5k store, copying, filtering and sorting costs about 0.8 ms.
- Over real HTTP, the list takes about 10 ms per request. A trivial `GET /shipments/:id` takes about 8 ms. At `limit=500` the list takes about 17 ms.
- Caching ETA per shipment was already tried and removed after QA saw stale ETAs following new events. It would save well under 1 ms here and bring that risk back.

**What I added**
- `test/shipments-list-perf.test.ts` seeds 5k shipments and checks three things:
  - The default page returns 50 items, each with an `eta`.
  - The average request time stays under 250 ms. That budget is deliberately loose so it won't flake on a slow CI box.
  - A new `exception` event changes the `eta` on the very next list request, so there's no stale ETA.
- I changed no source code. I recorded the findings in the ledger.

**What's still open**
The staging slowness is real but unexplained. It's probably something specific to staging, such as disk or log I/O on the Docker bind mount, response size, or a client calling with a large `limit`. To find it I'd need a profile from staging itself. It would help to know:
- The actual response time there.
- Which `limit` the callers use.
- Whether the request-log lines are slow to write.

I can add per-request timing logs (IDs only, no recipient data) to measure it on staging. Pagination is the other option.

# Ledger — parcel-tracker (Vienna warehouse shipment tracking; Node 24 runs TS directly, zero deps, no build)

## Rules (user)
- NEVER modify anything under src/legacy/ — vendored from old monolith; platform team's sync job overwrites it every Monday, so changes are silently lost.
- NO new npm deps, not even dev deps — each needs ~6-week security review.
- NEVER log recipient name/address/phone anywhere — GDPR; DPO flagged it in last month's audit. Shipment IDs + tracking numbers are OK.
- New user-facing error `message` fields in GERMAN (packers' UI shows them verbatim); `code` stays English SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE. Existing English messages were left as is.
- GET /shipments/:id response must stay byte-for-byte unchanged — mobile app v2.3 has a strict schema and crashes on unknown/missing fields; next release January. `eta` is only in GET /shipments list items (route-local, shared shipmentToApi untouched).
- docs/erp-api.md is owned by the ERP team: DO NOT edit. User fixes README port himself/herself.
- Work autonomously; user reviews everything at the end.

## Decisions (why)
- Holidays: hardcoded 2026+2027 list in src/services/holidays.ts — warehouse has no outbound internet, so no holiday API. Extend before 2028.
- Tracking validation: ONLY ATP gets UPU S10 check-digit validation (src/services/tracking.ts); other carriers accept any non-empty value — formats change often, last year valid DHL numbers were rejected for 2 days.
- ERP signing: HMAC-SHA256 hex, secret from env ERP_WEBHOOK_SECRET (unset => unsigned + one warning). Signature is a top-level `sig` body field over the body JSON without `sig`; sent last so stripping it reproduces the signed string. No header.
- ERP retries: 3 attempts total, FIXED 30 s, no backoff — ERP dedups by event_id only within 2 min. Only network errors/5xx retried. In-memory only (lost on restart); delay injectable.
- Store stays plain JSON (data/store.json), NO SQLite — ops' nightly rsync backup diffs plain text. Writes debounced 200 ms from first pending mutation; store.flush() on SIGINT/SIGTERM.
- ERP payload fields are event_type/occurred_at per docs (old type/at only accepted until 2026-12-31). `note` deliberately not sent: free text could contain recipient PII.
- Flaky test 'emits webhook on delivered' (test/events.test.ts), OPS-412, platform team owns it: if it fails rerun once, don't fix.

## Dead ends (don't retry)
- X-Signature header for ERP — API gateway strips all custom X- headers (found on staging).
- Batching ERP events (array of 50) — ERP answers 422 to any array; one event object per request (user tried Sept 2026).
- ETA memoization — QA saw stale ETA in the list after a new event, cache key got messy; removed (user). My version could not reproduce staleness. Plan: paginate GET /shipments later.
- fs.watch for config hot reload (future, nothing built) — never fires on staging (Docker bind mount from Windows host); fs.watchFile polling works (user).

## Facts
- ERP sandbox is on port 9911 since the Oct infra move, NOT 8080 (docs + README + config/default.json erp.url still say 8080; ERP_URL env overrides).
- Staging log logs/staging-2026-11-12.log contains recipient names/addresses on event lines; no code here writes them (cause unknown, DPO-relevant). Peak ERP load there: 2 notifications/min.
- data/fixtures/shipments.sample.json: 7 of 31 ATP numbers have wrong S10 check digits (would be rejected now); not fixed.
- Staging list slowness (5k shipments) is unexplained: ETA calc is only ~7 µs each, so it was not the cause.
- Shell quirk: two heredocs with backticks in one Bash call fail; use Write/Edit for files.

## Now
- Done, all UNCOMMITTED (nothing committed since 0f67fab), 94/94 tests pass, src/legacy + package.jso
